WHAT_IT_IS: Printed document on white paper.
WORDS:
My book of songs and poetry weights exactly thirteen pounds. What just that number mean in real life? Well, for example a pretty good-sized house cat would be around this weight. When my cat was in his prime he weighed around eleven pounds, that was ten years ago. My little black man now tips the scales at a mere seven pounds. The dude will have been my right-hand man for seventeen years in another month or so. That little BO-E-O has seen virtually my whole life. From seventh grade to high school graduation to college graduation all the way up to marriage. I don’t see any children coming for at least another four or five six or seven or eight years. I want to wait until I am financially stable before undertaking another dependent. Being a novel writer, a journalist, a poet, a song writer, a landscaper, carpenter, painter, and a husband I have never been especially great at specialization. Kind of like a typewriter machine repairer living in the age of the computer or another walking fossil… a legal landscaper. But I digress, there are a few things that I do specialize in and always pay careful attention to: My cat, my wife, my writing, my songs and most importantly my integrity.

The Big Ham (referenced to before as either little black man, the dude, or BO-E-O) is a long and slender, fixed male, short-haired, black cat. He’s pretty much as black as black can be; nose included. But if you look at Dude-a-roo in the light (and especially in direct sunlight) he isn’t black at all…… he turns red. As if he just came prancing out of some fancy pants Hollywood Salon after requesting the shampoo, blow dry with red highlights special advertised in the window. I’m staring at him right now and wherever there aren’t any shadows there is a vibrant red hue-filled glow upon his old and fading fur coat. We are poor and don’t have a lot of extra money to spent on heat. Living in Massachusetts during even Thanksgiving can get pretty cold and Dude-a-Rooski has been losing fur under his back legs and under his belly for about four or five years now. When we set the thermostat at 60 degrees he either jumps up onto the bed and curls up on the down comforter or else he’ll sit under his heat lamp on the couch.

The heat lamp is a creation from about ten years ago. When I was stretched out on my bed doing homework I used to have a little bendable lamp that I would use to shine light onto whatever I was reading. It had a light bulb shielded by a half-circled backing put there to direct the light down towards its heavier base. A flexible hose allowed the light head to be aimed into all different angles and directions. Well, one night I’m reading my history book and BO-E hops up onto my bed and sees me paying close attention to my studies and more specifically to my book. Since Little Dude loves to walk all over any and all paper that I am paying attention to he plops down right on top of my book. Directly under the lamp. Which shall from this point on forever be known as the heat lamp. When Slamma Lamma Hamma realized that this light created an impressive amount of heat he had found a new best friend.

My father’s side of the family has somehow all learned to handle the cold weather. His father and his father before him were Maine fishermen – a tough breed, indeed. Me? I’m a pussy when it comes to the cold but if you compare me to my cat then I look like a survivor of a nuclear explosion… I went all fifteen rounds, baby! Little Dude is the biggest whiner and complainer this side of the Mississippi River. He speaks when spoken to, and me and him, we talk a lot. I often call him Big Crying Ham in the morning for obvious reasons. He’s been a Big Ham for at least half of his life – ever since I realized that he loved being the center of attention when he was surrounded by familiar faces. He would always “ham it up” in front of the crowd. If you decided that you didn’t deem a cat worthy of acknowledgment then the Big Jerk would stand in front of
---
you and stare directly at you until he felt that you had properly acknowledged his presence. It was like he was royalty for heaven's sake. If you further refused he would bellow out a deep, "Meow!" with an added emphasis on the "Me" part in the beginning - staring at you all the while. And then he'd rub up against your leg. He never had to resort to any further actions because once he got to your leg there was never any way to resist him. Welcome to ancient Egypt. Egyptians worshipped cats and they worshipped the sun and here we have a cat who worshipped the sun (or else the heat lamp). He is under the heat lamp right now- the right side of his face glowing red fire and the left side coal black. So he's a cat who loves being warm...and he has a heat lamp that is plugged in for five months a year virtually 24 hours a day. It's just a perk of having a daddy who loves his little buddy. Mighty Ones, as my dad would call him, also has a door. In fact, he's had several.

"What would possess you to give a cat its own door?" It is certainly a logical question one might ask. Because I come from a long line of cold-house-people. Picture this scene: You are seventeen years old and you just got home from a day of high school. It's winter and you enter the door and you see that the thermostat tells you that the house is 58 degrees. You are cold as hell and your cat is screaming at you to acknowledge his presence. "Meow!" pause... "Meow!" silence. Have to pet the cat yet have to warm up quickly. Hmmm. So I turn up the house heat and we both run into the bathroom and shut the door. And turn on the red fluorescent heat lamp in the bathroom ceiling while also turning on the portable plug-in space heater and aiming it right in front of the toilet. The bathroom, being the smallest room of my father's house, also heated the quickest with the help of the added heat lamp up high and the heater down below. Once the seat had thawed for a moment I would proceed to sit down and go the bathroom and read the sports paper and Buddy Dudes would paw at the corner of my newspaper until he had a clear path to jump onto my lap. With the portable heater, which shall now be known only as "the heater" just a foot away from my legs the heat would start pouring up into the channel created by the toilet, myself and the unfolded newspaper I was reading. And we would be warm. Fifteen minutes later we could open the bathroom door and then we would no longer see our breath in the kitchen.

So with the cold house/warm bathroom relationship still fresh in our minds let us transfer a warm bathroom into a warm bedroom - mine. My father liked to keep the house at 60 degrees. At night he would put on his hooded sweatshirt, zip up his sleeping bag and sleep like a hiker. Meanwhile, my bedroom would have a heat lamp on as well as another space heater going full blast. Daddy called my room Miami. So you know who always slept with me...Dude. Well, once upon a time I got into a war of words with my father and ended up kicking my closed door open. It still shut but it wouldn't ever lock tight. Big Ham soon realized that all he had to do was to use his paw and pull against the bottom of my hollow, light door to make an easy escape from my room. The land of chow chow, also known as the kitchen, was just on the other side of this door. But it was cold out there. And Big Ham never once bothered to close the door. I put up with the excessive door openings for about a month - I'm a good daddy. But after the 543rd time it had to stop! I finally fixed the damn door but soon another problem arose...Scratch, scratch, scratch...."Meow!" Scratch, scratch, scratch..."ME-ow!" Now I had to get up and open the door to let him in and also to let him out. If I refused to let him out then he'd start staring at me. This went on for one week until it had to stop!

Alright, so we have a door. On one side of this door is a 75 degree room and on the other side is a 60 degree hallway. We have a cat that wants to go from one side to the other at absolutely any time he feels like. That cat wants to walk through walls.
---
Jesus Christ! Nobody's ever done that before. Hmmm... Let's see... Yeah, that would work... Brilliant! When I was finished I had cut a small rectangular, arched-at-the-top hole into the bottom part of my door that was just a little higher and wider than BO-E-O. To reduce drafts I had cut an old sweatshirt into vertical strips and hung them neatly just above the cut away entrance. Two or three layers of sweatshirt strips kept the bedroom pretty well insulated and Little Dude was free to enter and leave once he was convinced that he wouldn't bang his head upon poking through the hanging strips of fabric. And yes, it was fun shoving his little head through the little doorway the first couple of times in order to prove that there was no actual wood behind the covered opening. I had finished constructing my first kitty door for Dude.

The Dude's also got a sock full of drugs, at least three hoppers, one grizzly bear and a litter box that is so spatial that it has its own curtain. Yep, this is the life of the Big Ham.

Dear Kristin,
It is the tendency for a painter to paint with vivid colors. Just as it is natural for the accountant to deal with numbers. And poets, you might ask?...well they deal with imagery and symbolism. You were a symbol of purity and kindness. You provided me with a beacon of hope to which I could look to for support through the many dark tunnels that I have found myself lurking in. You have a set role in my life, a role from which you could never deviate from. You are support and a helping hand. In times of trouble and uneasiness you are there to comfort me. It is natural for me to make you into something that you are not or see you only as an ideal or an idol but reality must over take my poetic nature at sometime or another. This is a good time.
I used you to help myself and I realize that there is only a certain level that you can take me to. The rest I must go myself. Well you have taken me far and have led me to the gates of heaven. Now I must find my own way to sneak in. Perhaps when God is sleeping I can hop the fence?
I still have a little trouble with religious imagery. I am my own god and I do not follow his plan I make my own. If my actions are right and correct then I shall make myself a good life, if I screw up then I have no one to blame but myself. i live a life of no excuses anymore. I will not allow myself to wait forever for a plan that may or may not be guided by a hand above. I look for god in people and then follow them to a heaven on earth. It seems to be the safest bet for a doubting Thomas like me. As the Christians say I must not be charmed by false idols or worship false Gods. You used to be my link to God. Somewhere along the way you turned into God himself...And I think that would get us both in trouble in the eyes of the big guy. I have separated you two. With every word typed I see a clearer picture of the difference between you two. It has finally sunk in.

WHAT_IT_IS: A printed piece of paper.
WORDS:
Hello,
I called you but you weren't home. As I stood waitingly listening to the receiver, my heart beat with the same rhythm as the ringing of the unanswered phone. With each new ring I began to feel my happiness fade for it meant that each ring brought me father away from the sweet sunshine of your voice. The initial excitement that swept through me like a summer breeze through an open window dulled to a stagnance of a coffin, dark and void of hope. I reassured myself that you were just getting out of your car when I called or perhaps out of earshot when the phone last rang. Clinging to my hopes, like a child dreams of pokemon on Christmas morning, i called again. Again, as I heard each successive ring I pretended that you were walking in the door at that very moment. We are so close that I knew that you could feel me thinking of you. I imagined your footsteps running feverishly towards the phone in eager anticipation of the loved one who awaited. I held on and held on until the sound of the monotonous, busy ringing next to my ear saddened me to the harsh reality that you were not home. I collected myself and attempted to put forth a happy nature even though my insides were churning and my heart felt like an empty vessel, from which the blood that let it live had been painfully drained. My soul had escaped during the saddening rings of the call and was now searching for the love it once had known. It was searching for its place, its hope and its inspiration...My soul was searching for you. I set out to find my soul myself but I know deep down inside that I will only find it when I find you.

RUMORS FROM HEAVEN
Now that there's rock n' roll in heaven
Everyone enjoys the hymns
And the only problem that the church has
Is getting everybody in

Hard to tell just how the conversation sounds
When John's head is just about to hit the ground
As the echo of Jerry starts from the corner of the room
Playing long after dark as the echo finds its way around
All the while Jim is already out cold
He bought the ticket but the ride is getting old

The creator never really had a chance
For his disciples could no longer walk straight
The power of song and dance
Unleashed after ages inside the Golden Gate

These guys all got the same room upstairs
And thought their landlord is god still no one seems to care
Sit and scratch their heads wondering
Just who'll come knocking next
Yet time has told them that it's anyone's guess

Everybody's grateful to be dead
Because now they're the house band in Heaven
They sell out every single night
Now that doesn't sound too upsetting

Hey John, it's George who's been knocking at the door
Because of course Paul would've rang the bell
John responded that George must've left the Maharishi
Or else I figured we'd a seen him in hell

There goes Jimi playing again without his hands
Wearing only his headband and his funky underpants
Hey Jerry, go get a bucket of cold water
Let's see if we can get him outta this trance

He's sure can tap dance and he don't eat much
But when Elvis Presley's knocking don't ever let him in
For he'll just eat all of the chips and dip - what a sin
But Sinatra's okay 'cause he always brings gin

Hey who invited Bobby Dylan?
You know we're not allowed to let anyone in early
Keith Richards came all the way up for nothing
But we're sure we'll see him again shortly

John whispers...
No you ain't gonna see what I got in my pocket
But the words that come to me are knock it off and stop it
You want to change your ways but just what's the use?
I have far beyond my years too much pain and abuse

Jim wakes up mumbling something odd...
The day revolves around the tears
That come falling from the serpent's eyes
I hold the pain of the world inside my mind
Because my ears can no longer hear a child cry
My senses crawl beneath my skin
As a man once saw all becomes blind

But they all know George is not the type to be out done
The pressure of the sky falls on your back
The clouds start laughing in your face
The weather changes all the time
So remove your soul within its case

I wasn't placed on this earth just to entertain you... I'm here to spread knowledge as well. When my wife told me that she didn't know three people from this poem I decided that I had better make a handy reference guide. For all of us who are familiar with all of these characters I tried to throw out a few interesting nuggets of information here and there just to keep you reading. Generally speaking, the younger you are more you'll need it.
The other reason I made this list is because the poem gets better with knowledge. For instance, take the last two verses of the poem (this one is more of a song, actually): "Once you get your wings you don't have to walk up the stairway to get to heaven... Don't have to go chasing a band that is never on the run." You should also know that Paul McCartney was in a band called "Wings" and in 1973 they had an album entitled "Band on the Run." You should also know that another great rock band from the 1970s named Led Zeppelin came out with a song entitled "Stairway to Heaven." It's a great song. With all of this "new" information presented to you those two lines just became a whole lot better. In the same sense, Sammy Davis Jr. was a very skinny black man who used to tap dance a lot. There are just so many little joke references in this poem in particular that I thought it would be helpful to do this. I got the idea from my commentary on Four Wars: a poem that mentions many figures from history... if you don't know your history then you don't completely understand the poem (and subsequently don't comprehend my greatness in its entirety. He he).
I got the idea for this poem because I was depressed that most of my favorite rockers were dead. I started picturing them all in heaven just sort of hanging out. I thought that it would make for a pretty interesting story so I ran with it. I even tried to write some of the lyrics in a few of the character's own style of writing or thinking. I do a pretty good Jim Morrison impersonation if I do say so myself. Anyone who is about fifty-years-old should get a kick out of this one. I hope you enjoyed it.

Politician Blues
Someday I'll be famous and everyone'll know my name
(of course I'll change it first though)
Someday I'll be a star with all this fortune and fame
(I probably won't like that much though)
It all starts now and it all starts here
I sing real loud so my message is clear
Be yourself, do what you gotta do
Life is tough but somehow I know you'll make it through
If you don't like me then this don't apply to you
There's a new path unpaved so its up to you
We all follow the leader- you do it too
It can't be that way anymore
Time for us to settle the score
Start pushing the old values aside
No more can we go run and hide
The government that rules us, everyone is a liar
Word's catching on and now its spreading like a fire
They've talked enough nothin' more they can say
Follow me and I'll show you the way
Goin' to Washington D.C.
Time to meet the true enemy
Their twisting toungues will tell you its me
Don't listen to them if you want to be free
Join us- every color and race
Speed up! We've got to quicken the pace!
Million man march (HUH!) multiply that by ten
History, we're goin' through it again
Do it for the homeless you meet
Do it for the children on the street
Think about the hungry, the ill and the sick
We'll dismantle the system brick by brick
I tell it straight and don't beat around the bush
We tried to pull now its time to push
It's nine for them and one for us
It's their time to sit in the back of the bus
The politicians look us right in the eyes
While their words are full of lies
---

They tell me because when I ask why

I'm going to give each one a mirror

I'm going to run for president
So I can show what's so evident
I will answer questions truthfully
And they can think what they want of me
I'll hide behind no mask at all
Not forced to sit I will stand tall
I'll be myself, I won't wear no vail
I smoked pot and I INHALED
I don't hide what I don't understand
What do you expect? I'm a simple man
I don't mean to bring you all the bad news
Only the story of the politician blues

CLINICAL DEPRESSION
Parents: She finds a bottle of pills and she holds them in her hand
Daughter: My whole world is falling down and noone understands
There's one way to solve my problems-thats for me to go away
After I'm placed down in my grave I can't hear anyone say:
Parents: She had the whole world in her hand but she only let us down
Now she's gone too far away and she's only six feet under ground
What could make her think that we didn't love her so?
What could make her think that there was no place left to go?
Daughter: I'm sorry mom, I'm sorry dad
I hoped that this would make you glad
I couldn't bare to see your face
When you thought your love's a waste
I didn't want to hurt you nor cause you any pain
I guess I imagined my loss would be your gain
That would pass just like the moon with just a hug and kiss
This is your one mistake that'll never be undone
We used to have two children, now we're left with one
Everybody stumbles when they learn to talk
Everybody mumbles when they learn to walk
One thing we've learned with wisdom is you give it your best sho
We prayed you'd be strong but you barely even faught
Did you ever listen to anything we'd taught?
When you swim against the tide you give it all you got
Daughter: With your expectations oh so high you nailed me to the wall
I ended up laying down when I tried to stand too tall
Whenever I try to shift to a higher gear I always seem to stall
When I needed you the most I was too afraid to call
Parents: Oh how did we miss the truth with the writing on the wall?
Why did you say nothing? We should have known it all
If only you had told us for we can be so blind
If only we had known we would have been more kind
Daughter: What have I done? This shouldn't have been my fate
Now its so dark I guess its time to sleep
I realize I've only made one mistake and now its far too late
I'll be here for an eternity and all I'll do is weep
Parents: Always remember that you're daddy's little girl
---
The world would've been your oyester and you its pearl
I would do anything to give you a second chance
I'd trade my soul to let you have just one last dance
You were my daughter and you were my friend
If only you had known that it didn't have to end

WORDS:
ALISON'S AIRPLANE
I find my religion in the basement of churches
Never mind a pew

Here I sit trying to learn from my mistakes
God knows I've made a few

If you'd made as many as I have
Then you'd probably sit here too

Here I sit and reminisce it all
Biding my time by reading
Slogans on the wall

A higher power is what I need
Something above myself can set me free

You can only tell what you're really worth
When you realize that you're not the center of the earth

The sun does not rise for you
No matter how much you want it to

Gravity was made for many reasons
Something to do with the sun, the moon
And the changing of the seasons

It may be true that it pulls you down
But in order to walk the road ahead
First your feet must meet the ground

Then the rest is up to you
Use your better judgment if you want to
From which you came

If you choose to walk back down the road
Don't point your finger at me
That finger of blame

Alison told me she had an airplane
Of course I didn't believe it
So I asked her to teach me how to fly
But she told me I couldn't see it
---
She said if you want to go for a ride

NAME: MAYBE SOMEDAY
WHAT_IT_IS: The item consists of printed text on a white sheet of paper.
COLLECTION_SOURCE: wiring sheet V1 CATEGORIES (clean names) + item 1966 SORTED BY CATEGORIES lists (title exact on card, window 52)
AGE_DATE_BASIS: HIGH: POEMS BY TOM HIGH (BK-01 2007-12-11) (poem date; this sheet may be a later printout)
WORDS:
MAYBE SOMEDAY

Maybe someday my wounds will mend
Maybe someday their laws will bend
Darkness has slowly become my best friend
Been trying everything but this feeling won't end
Confusion is my brother, I'm the son of desperation
Lost is my desire and I'm still searching for motivation
I've put everything off until the end of time
My friends think they're psychics trying to read my mind
I tell 'em you can't read blank paper with only blue lines
The traffic lights are red and stop reads every sign
I only see things blurly, no better than the blind
People ask how I'm doing and of course I tell 'em I'm doing fine
I want to scream at them even though they're being kind
I wish I could tell them the truth but I just don't feel inclined

Every morning I wake up and I pray I can stay in bed
Sleep is so peaceful and so good for the head
I got to think positive - that's what the doctor said
The best I can do is that soon I'll be dead
When I told Dr. Kevorkian he didn't wanna see me no more
He shook my hand as he kicked me out the door

Now I'm sitting on the corner with my coffee and cigarette in my hand
A lady passing by threw change in my cup and said "Sorry kid but I understand"
So I drank my coffee and almost choked on a dime
I imagine I'll be feeling like this until the end of time

Just then I saw a beautiful and I took her by the hand
I said "Please come with me away from this harsh land"
But she must be foreign for she didn't understand
Why is it, life never turns out the way you planned?

I bought a newspaper because I needed some good news
Took one look at the cover and kept singin' the blues
All this mayhem and murder just made me feel even worse
Five men died in an car accident including the driver of a hurst
I'm part of the problem- when you hear this you ain't gonna feel any better
---
Hopefully it'll be sunny and my life will change like the weather
It's always raining and the clouds never want to pass by
When things are this bad why do I even try?

I'm stuck in this place with no money and a car that won't run
If I ever get a new one I'm driving out the rain and finding the sun
A car with a CD player and Bob Dylan on the stage
To a place where I can have a wife and a kid and die of old age
Maybe someday I'll be free of this rage
Maybe someday I'll be free of this cage
Maybe someday empty won't read the gauge
Maybe someday God's hand will turn the page
Maybe someday I'll have it made
Maybe someday......it's just not today

MAYBE SOMEDAY

A PERFECT WORLD

The whole world's a fight I can't get no peace
My mind gets disrupted when it's at ease
Watching the sunrise is a long forgotten art
Feet so busy walking separate from the heart
When was the last time you noticed the moon?
I'm surprised you've forgotten so soon
There's so much more than what you've been told
Rise up in rebellion, could you be so bold?

This set pattern you follow is just one of their lies
A world lacking communion, only me's and I's
Through competition our brotherhood has been broken
As no one's acknowledged these words that I've spoken
Everything, even people, filed by order and rank
Number one built the Titanic yet down it sank
There's still time left to return these ideas you've been sold
Rise up in rebellion, could you be so bold?

Some say if winning isn't everything than why keep score?
Those same people send other mother's sons to war
I could be like you or maybe someone else
One step towards them and one away from myself
Sometimes they see me and ask me "How I feel?"
I respond "A hamster on a hamster's wheel"
If you feel trapped like a rat in this world so cold
Rise up in rebellion, could you be so bold?

I'll keep on fighting no matter what's in store
But at least I'll know what I'm fighting for
My own little peace and quiet in this world so vast
This world makes me dizzy because it's moving to fast
Round and round they go as they spin their wheels
Trying hard to keep their poker face on when the dealer deals
Stop going for broke when you'll win if you hold
Rise up in rebellion, could you be so bold?

The brokers in the suits and ties walking down Wall Street
The ones with the diamond watches and their hair so neat
They get so stressed out playing all their Wall Street games
They get home and yell at their wives and forget their own kid's names
All for the love of money and nothing more
If they call that rich then you can call me poor
If they tell you the lie 'all that glitters is gold'
Rise up in rebellion, could you be so bold?

As I climb up the mountains or float over the sea
I find myself alone and contented and alive and free
No need to look at my watch or punch a clock
And I notice my feet when I go for a walk
It could be like this if enough people believe
Just as the wind blows a flower, I'm planting my seed
The time has come for us to break the mold
Rise up in rebellion, could we be so bold?

Title: contradictory

Stanza 1: people are so busy they never take the time to appreciate being alive or the little things in life that are so beautiful like nature or something as simple as a sunrise or the moon. We’re all taught to go, go, go when sometimes its better to just sit and observe. We need to change the way we live our daily lives. But it does take a lot to change.

Stanza 2: Everything is one big competition: school, job, driving (everybody is in a hurry) everyone compares everyone else by how much money they make. The constant competition breaks down society and social relations. Yet we’re taught this through and through – be it deliberately or not. We always have to be better than the next guy. The best ship builder built the Titanic so being number one isn’t a guaranteed success.

Stanza 3: Some are so bent out of shape over numbers (grades or money) that they think that’s why you do something for a 100 or an A but you do it for yourself. The author (me) isn’t like that (let’s pretend) and wants others to see the error of their ways. He doesn’t want to give in to their way, that’s why he tells the audience to rebel. The reference to the hamster wheel means that everyone’s going around and around at a million miles an hour but for what purpose? Stop and relax and enjoy life – you only live once.

Stanza 4: The author won’t give in. The world isn’t what he wants it to be but he’ll keep remembering and searching for his perfect ideals. The poker face reference shows that they know the error of their ways but since everyone else does it they do it too. They don’t have to go for broke or be so extreme in working 40 – 50 – 60 – 70 hours a week. They work so much they lose sight of what’s important like family, love and happiness. A happy medium of less work and more play and more appreciation is much better yet it is not the general way of thinking – it is extreme.

Stanza 5: The stock brokers represent the rich people who work so much and care for money the most. They represent the worst case of the problem; anti-author. AROUND THE KING'S TABLE

All raise glasses to propose a toast
Tilt back brims to honor a host

Raise glass to lips to praise the day
Lifting a hand as all guests say:

"This man who sits at table head
Who sits before us breaking bread

The finest king throughout the land
Deserves a toast so raise a hand"

As we sit around the table
We laugh away the night

We drink for as long as we're able
And toast glasses for all that's right

A toast to our tongue which tastes our drinks
And to our brains that swim and think

A toast for grapes which are used for wine
Raise cups for livers, both yours and mine

Drink a taste to honor waste
Of dribbled wine spilled on your face

A toast for chairs on which we sit
Give thanks for thrones on which we shit

Before we sleep and go to bed
Upon light pillow with heavy head

Let us toast that tomorrow
Shall be the same as today

So far away from sorrow
That toast again we may

Poem 1
Hidden Evils

A crying teen wonders how much more she can handle
While mangy dogs dig through trash and howl at the wind
The priest in the church lights a holy candle
For all of his lost children who have sinned

Son lays awake all night dreaming of tomorrow
Grandmother prays for her soul to be saved
Father works his second job, eyes full of sorrow
Single mother wonders how the bills will get paid

A child born of racists, his heart fills with hate
Paint chips off the walls of the liquor store
An abandoned building becomes home to a family of eight
The donation bin stays empty while collecting for the poor

A pigeon wanders aimlessly unsure of where to look for food
A wrinkled and ripped newspaper blows around in the park
A homeless man sleeping on a bench awakes in a foul mood
As night falls all that’s wrong with the world is covered by dark

This poem was an attempt to break my rhyming pattern of consecutive twos. I
am also a fan of this rhyming scheme because it is a little harder for me because
I’m not used to it. I tried to show all the evils in the world that we, as a society,
have a tendency to overlook because they’re commonplace. I started by only
rhyming in the 2nd and 4th verses but didn't like the end result so I redid the other
two lines so that they rhymed.

Poem 1
This is a first draft. It is about my own piece of sanity. A future revision may include lengthening the piece. This poem was inspired by a Pete Townsend tune of the same harmony. I was feeling very stressed and I needed a way to put things in perspective. This did the trick.

SYMPHONY IN MY HEAD
There is a symphony playing in my mind
And it only plays for me
Sometimes I try to write it down
Though it somehow remains free
So pure and true
No pen or paper could ever hold
The only thing that's mine
That I hold in this world so cold
Sometimes the music sounds
When life has got me down
It's the only thing that awakes me from my sorrow
Sometimes the music plays
When my happiness goes away
Reminds me there's always hope for tomorrow

Poem 2
This poem was inspired after I was playing around with some catch phrases. I came up with the catch phrase and wrote the rest of the poem around the concept of "You can call it fate." The rest will be here someday, I hope. This poem ponders over the question of why bad things happen. I think it would be better served with 2 more lines in each stanza.
This is the second draft and a future draft would include the last stanza concluding with the defendant commiting a bad crime.

CALL IT FATE
Birds circle around your home
One more time won't they leave you alone
They flap their wings from side to side
From Mother Nature no man can hide
Being punished for crimes - well, that may be
Crimes against humanity
Just when you though there was no one to see
Now look at your life and who's to blame?
You can call it fate
What a shame?

As your family boasts "You're in the prime of your life"
You go under the doctor's knife
For cancer has no name or face
Unfortunately for you its too late
Enter the hospital a dying life
Exit the church a crying wife

Poem 4
This is a second draft. This poem was inspired by random thoughts of the uncountable amounts of idiots that this world has to offer. I am good with people yet on a whole I hate humans. I am the type that cheers at plane crashes and killing sprees. This is a taste of my anti-people (especially worthless people) mentality:

PATCHING THE HOLE

There’s no parking spaces
Only unhappy faces
Untied shoelaces
Now I’ve covered all the bases

Puddles of grime
The offspring of slime
For whom the great bells chime
Whose horrors cannot be covered by rhyme

Thoughts like feet buried in cement
On the mind reads space for rent
If only could a conscience be lent
Wasted space - wasted time spent

Cannot fix the flaw - only patch the hole
The potential of diamonds results in coal
Able to race the race though blind to the goal
Only glimpses and pieces never the whole

Never a reasonable thought about why they’re here
Ignorance replaces fear
The voice of reason they’re unable to hear
Never aware of how far away or near

The truth of it all they could never bear
Answer half-witted responses of life’s not fair
Entering every endeavor without much care
Rise above the filth - if you dare?

Poem 5
This is a first draft - I like heat, I hate snow. Tough times are ahead for winter is here. 
Winter is here and depression sets in. No more beautiful girls running around in beautiful bikini’s and no more warm days. Everybody gets like this when the summer fades away yet few people write it down. I may include a stanza after this one titled summer of the living and make it a comparison piece but I’m still thinking.

WINTER OF THE DEAD

Dying leaves fall from trees
Harsh winds blow as rivers freeze
Birds escape to warmer places
Red cheeks glisten on children’s faces
---
Now look at death and who's to blame?
You can call it fate
You can call it a shame

In the next room of the hospital is a mother's joy
The prize of a life - a baby boy
Parents counted the fingers and counted the toes
But what's in the soul nobody really knows
Food, shelter and love - baby got his fill
But no one knows why he grew to kill
You can look at their deaths and who they blame
You can call it fate
You can call it a shame

A man dresses in the mirror and he flashes a smile
In a two-thousand dollar suit he'll wear at the trial
He asks the judge to cut his client a break
Starts preaching about how we all make mistakes
The judge, on these words, reduces bail
Keeps a guilty man away from jail
Freedom gained but is anything lost?
Will he do it again?
They keep their fingers crossed

Poem 3
This is a first draft. This poem was inspired by the turtle that my mom got from my girlfriend. My mom is nuts and she spent a ton of money to keep this turtle alive after a ton medical problems. The average person would have let the turtle play in the street in traffic. Now the turtle lives in an empty glass bowl with daily swims of about an hour in duration. A pointless existence in my eyes. I always wondered how the turtle sees things:

THE TRUTH ABOUT TURTLES

To live one day outside this glass
Even if next I come to pass
I dream of the day of being free
Your life be meaningless if you were me
A fairy tale...once upon a time I swam around
Presently no rock, nor blue sky, can be found
To big cat sitting close I appear as a meal
Every time I untuck my head their eyes I feel
From five sides of invisible walls free me please
While sixth lies open, such a tease
Perhaps I should grow white wings so wide
To free me, release me, from where I reside
And teeth so sharp to bite through screen
Fly back to my home - alone and unseen
To my rock on my pond where I used to sleep
Where I was trapped and sold by nets that creep
Yes, death or liberty
Anything but this
Freedom for my sons and my daughters
And the family I miss

stories.

Established in April, 1985, The Middlesex County Driving Under the Influence of Liquor (DUIL) Program provides an alternative to incarceration for the O.U.I. offender. It is a 14-day residential treatment program consisting of individual and group counseling, education, physical fitness and an introduction to self-help programs.

To date, we have served over 16,200 clients from 35 District Courts throughout Massachusetts.

The program is founded upon the premise that alcoholism is a treatable disease and that the majority of O.U.I. second offenders suffer from this illness.

The program provides a structured environment at a minimum security level in which clients experience clear boundaries and limits on their behavior. Prescribed standards of conduct and restrictions of freedom are intended as a means of self-discipline in the hope that clients will learn to establish appropriate boundaries in other social settings once discharged from the program.

The total cost of the program is $812 at $58/day. Payment plans are available if a client cannot pay in one lump sum. Such an arrangement increases the total cost of $880.

Over 40 hours of substance abuse and mental health education is provided, including extensive coverage of HIV/AIDS issues as they relate to substance abuses.

Each client is seen individually at least four times and participates in a minimum of 27 hours of group therapy.

*Each client will be assigned to an outpatient aftercare agency for follow-up treatment. If a client's probation officer assigns them to aftercare prior to attending D.U.I.L. the client will continue at that agency upon discharge*.

If a client does not pay the full fee upon admission and is placed on our payment plan, all moneys owed must be paid before a client receives credit for completing the program. Our payment plan includes a carrying charge. Visa or Master card are welcome.

There is no public transportation directly to this facility. Clients are advised to arrange for a ride to and from the program.

Clients must report at scheduled time. Late arrivals will be returned to the court.

Smoking is severely restricted. Noncompliance with our smoking policy will result in immediate discharge.

No visitors.

No incoming phone calls - pay phones are available on the unit for outgoing calls during free time.

All reschedules and other changes relevant to admission must be done through your probation officer only.
